title: RAPTOR: Role-Aware Private Training for Mixture-of-Experts
abstract: arXiv:2609.05770v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Differentially private (DP) fine-tuning methods treat sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models as a single dense block, ignoring that shared layers see all data while experts only see routed records. We identify and formally characterize three resulting failure modes: global clipping suppresses expert gradients, batch-level normalization dilutes sparse expert updates, and fixed privacy noise degrades signal-to-noise ratio on low-load experts. We introduce RAPTOR - a Role-Aware Private Training framework, which alternates shared and expert optimization and targets each failure directly, using expert-specific clipping and noise together with a public expected-owner denominator and a count-independent update schedule that avoids conditioning on private, realized expert counts. We prove the resulting mechanism satisfies $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-DP: because each record is assigned to exactly one owner expert, per-expert mechanisms within a layer

translated_title: RAPTOR：面向混合专家模型的角色感知隐私训练
translated_abstract: 差分隐私（DP）微调方法将稀疏的混合专家模型视为单个密集整体，忽略了共享层能看到所有数据、而专家只能看到被路由到自己的记录这一差异。我们识别并正式刻画了由此产生的三种失效模式：全局梯度裁剪会抑制专家梯度、批次级归一化会稀释稀疏的专家更新、固定的隐私噪声会降低低负载专家的信噪比。我们提出了RAPTOR——一个角色感知的隐私训练框架，它交替进行共享层和专家层的优化，并直接针对每种失效模式，采用专家特定的裁剪与噪声，结合一个公共的期望所有者分母以及与专家计数无关的更新计划，从而避免以私有的、实际实现的专家计数为条件。我们证明了所得机制满足$(\varepsilon,\delta)$-差分隐私：由于每条记录被恰好分配给一个所有者专家，层内的各专家机制……
tldr: RAPTOR提出了一种角色感知的差分隐私训练框架，通过专家特定的裁剪与噪声、公共期望所有者分母和计数无关的更新计划，解决了现有DP微调方法在稀疏MoE模型上的三种失效模式，同时保持(ε,δ)-DP保证。
en_tdlr: RAPTOR introduces a role-aware differentially private training framework for sparse MoE models that directly addresses three failure modes of conventional DP fine-tuning via expert-specific clipping and noise, a public expected-owner denominator, and count-independent update schedules, while preserving (ε,δ)-DP guarantees.
